plan.contextChunk: This figure lays out a multichannel convolution as one symbolic equation joining three groups of tensors drawn in offset perspective. On the left, under the bold label w, sit two stacks of light blue square grids, each three sheets deep; a tall brace at the far left reads C_out filters and spans both stacks, a small brace above the upper stack reads C_in, and braces along the right side and the bottom edge of the lower stack each read K for the filter's two spatial extents. A star operator separates the filter bank from the middle group, labeled x_in, a much larger pink grid also drawn as three offset sheets, with a brace above reading C_in and a brace beneath its width reading M. An equals sign leads to the right-hand group, labeled x_out, a single pink grid whose upper brace reads C_out and whose right-hand brace reads N. Color keeps the learned parameters distinct from the data, and the braces let the reader match dimensions straight across the operator: the filter bank's depth agrees with the input's C_in, while the number of filters becomes the output's C_out. The drawing spells out shape bookkeeping that is easy to lose track of in symbols alone.

elements: left group label 'w' (bold) above the filter bank
filter bank: C_out stacks of light-blue square grids (default 2 stacks), each stack C_in=3 sheets deep
each blue sheet is a K×K grid of cells (default K=3) with visible grid lines
tall left brace spanning all blue stacks labelled 'C_out filters'
small upper brace over the top blue stack labelled 'C_in'
right-side brace on the lower blue stack labelled 'K' (vertical extent)
bottom brace under the lower blue stack labelled 'K' (horizontal extent)
star convolution operator '⋆' between filter bank and input
middle group label 'x_in' (bold) above the input tensor
input tensor: pink grid drawn as C_in=3 offset sheets, each sheet M×M (M=7) with grid lines
upper brace over x_in labelled 'C_in'
bottom brace under x_in labelled 'M'
highlighted K×K receptive-field patch on the front sheet of x_in (outline + tint)
equals sign '=' between input and output
right group label 'x_out' (bold) above the output tensor
output tensor: pink grid drawn as C_out offset sheets (default 2), each sheet N×N (N=7) with grid lines
upper brace over x_out labelled 'C_out'
right-side brace on x_out labelled 'N'

interactions.label: C_out (number of filters)
interactions.teaches: Each blue filter stack produces exactly one pink output sheet: raising C_out adds a blue stack on the left and a matching sheet on the right, making the one-filter-to-one-output-channel mapping explicit

interactions.label: Kernel size K
interactions.teaches: Changes the spatial footprint of every blue filter and the highlighted receptive patch on x_in, clarifying that K is the local window size while M is the full input width

interactions.label: Slide kernel over input
interactions.teaches: The K×K×C_in window sweeps across x_in and writes one value per position into x_out, turning the static shape bookkeeping into the actual sliding-window computation
Reveals the dimension braces (C_in, C_out, K, M, N) on demand so the reader can match depths and extents straight across the ⋆ and = operators without permanent clutter

demo_steps.title: Default shapes
demo_steps.narration: Two blue filter stacks (C_out=2), each 3 sheets deep (C_in) and 3×3 (K), convolve a 3-channel 7×7 input to give a 2-sheet 7×7 output. Match the C_in depth of the filters to the C_in depth of x_in.

demo_steps.title: More output channels
demo_steps.narration: Raise C_out to 4: four blue stacks appear on the left and the pink x_out gains two more sheets. Every filter yields exactly one output channel.

demo_steps.title: Larger receptive field
demo_steps.narration: Raise K to 5: each blue grid and the highlighted patch on x_in grow to 5×5, while M stays 7 — the local window is now most of the input width.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Layout along +X (screen-right): filter bank centered near x=-6, x_in near x=0, x_out near x=+6; star at x≈-3, equals at x≈+3. Oblique depth: successive sheets of every tensor offset by (+0.18 X, +0.18 Y, +0.30 Z) to mimic the source's up-right receding copies; C_in=3 sheets per blue stack and per x_in, C_out sheets for x_out. Cell size 0.42 world units, so a K×K sheet spans K*0.42 and M×M / N×N sheets span 7*0.42≈2.94. Blue fill #cfe8f5 with edge #6fa8cf; pink fill #f6dada with edge #d49a9a; grid lines #333; braces/labels/operators black #111. Highlighted receptive patch on the front x_in sheet: outline #e05a2b width 2 plus 0.25-opacity orange tint over the K×K cells at the current slide position. N=M=7 (same-padding) so the output sheet size matches the source; only the highlight and blue footprint respond to K. Whole scene fits roughly X∈[-8,8], Y∈[-2,2.5], Z∈[0,1.2].
interactionPlan.notes: Build each tensor as a Group of C PlaneGeometry sheets with a GridHelper-like line overlay, offset in Z for the oblique stack; rebuild groups reactively when cOut or kernelK change (dispose old geometry). Keep the slide animation as a moving highlight rectangle + tinted cells on the front x_in sheet and a synchronized filled cell cursor on the front x_out sheet; pause it implicitly when the user drags kernelK to avoid conflicting motion. Render braces as screen-space sprites or thin tube curves that always face the camera so labels stay legible under the oblique pose; tie their visibility to the dimLabels hover. Use MeshBasicMaterial (no lighting) to keep the flat textbook look.

evaluation.notes: The figure correctly represents the convolution operation with proper grid sizes, colors, stacking, and layout; the main weakness is that dimension braces/labels are hidden by default rather than always visible as in the source, though the toggle and kernel-slide animation add good pedagogical value.

Consider making the oblique angle slightly more pronounced to better match the source's 3D appearance
